definition: To invite someone on a date.
examples: He wants to ask out his coworker.
Are you going to ask him out?
She was asked out by a guy from work.

spanish.definition: Invitar a alguien a una cita.

definition: To support someone; to make a copy of computer files; to move backward.
examples: Back up your files every week.
My friends backed me up.
Can you back up the car a little?

spanish.definition: Apoyar a alguien; copiar archivos; moverse hacia atrás.

definition: To explode; to fill with air; to get very angry.
examples: The car blew up.
Let's blow up some balloons.
He blew up at me for no reason.

spanish.definition: Estallar; llenar de aire; enojarse mucho.

definition: To phone someone who called you.
examples: I'll call back in five minutes.
She never called back.
Can you ask him to call back later?

spanish.definition: Llamar a alguien que te llamó.

definition: To cancel.
examples: They called off the game because of rain.
The wedding was called off.
We're calling off the meeting.

spanish.definition: Suspender algo.

definition: To become less angry or excited.
examples: Calm down and tell me what happened.
It took her an hour to calm down.
The baby is calming down now.

spanish.definition: Volverse menos enojado o alterado.

definition: To reach someone ahead of you; to talk about recent news.
examples: Walk slowly so I can catch up.
Let's get coffee and catch up.
She caught up with the others.

spanish.definition: Llegar hasta alguien que va adelante; hablar de lo reciente.

definition: To arrive and register at a hotel or an airport.
examples: We checked in at the hotel at three.
You must check in two hours before your flight.
Are you checking in today?

spanish.definition: Llegar y registrarse en un hotel o un aeropuerto.

definition: To leave a hotel and pay; to look at something.
examples: We checked out at noon.
Check out this cool video!
I'm checking out the new store.

spanish.definition: Irse de un hotel y pagar; mirar algo.

definition: To become happier, or to make someone happier.
examples: Cheer up! It's not that bad.
The flowers cheered her up.
He's trying to cheer up his friend.

spanish.definition: Ponerse más feliz, o alegrar a alguien.

definition: To make a place clean and tidy.
examples: Clean up your room!
We cleaned up after the party.
He's cleaning up the kitchen.

spanish.definition: Dejar un lugar limpio y ordenado.

definition: Used to tell someone to hurry or to try; to start working.
examples: Come on, we're late!
The lights came on.
Come on, you can do it!

spanish.definition: Se usa para apurar o animar a alguien; empezar a funcionar.

definition: To draw a line through a word.
examples: Cross out the wrong answer.
She crossed out his name.
He's crossing out words in his essay.

spanish.definition: Trazar una línea sobre una palabra.

definition: To do less of something; to make a tree fall.
examples: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.
They cut down the old tree.
She's cutting down on coffee.

spanish.definition: Hacer menos de algo; tumbar un árbol.

definition: To stop a supply; to separate.
examples: They cut off our electricity.
The town was cut off by the snow.
Sorry, we got cut off.

spanish.definition: Detener un suministro; separar.

definition: To visit someone for a short time.
examples: Drop by anytime.
She dropped by after work.
I'll drop by tomorrow.

spanish.definition: Visitar a alguien por un rato corto.

definition: To stop going to school or stop doing something.
examples: He dropped out of college.
She dropped out of the race.
Many students are dropping out.

spanish.definition: Dejar de ir a la escuela o de hacer algo.

definition: To eat at a restaurant.
examples: Let's eat out tonight.
We ate out three times last week.
They're eating out for her birthday.

spanish.definition: Comer en un restaurante.

definition: To break into pieces; to stop working well.
examples: My old shoes are falling apart.
Their marriage fell apart.
The plan fell apart at the last minute.

spanish.definition: Romperse en pedazos; dejar de funcionar bien.

definition: To fall to the ground.
examples: The little boy fell down.
Be careful, or you'll fall down.
The old fence fell down in the storm.

spanish.definition: Caer al suelo.

definition: To write information in the spaces on a form; to do someone's job for a time.
examples: Fill in your name and address.
Can you fill in for me tomorrow?
She's filling in the blanks.

spanish.definition: Escribir datos en los espacios de un formulario; hacer el trabajo de alguien por un tiempo.

definition: To complete a form.
examples: Please fill out this form.
I filled out the application online.
He's filling out his tax forms.

spanish.definition: Completar un formulario.

definition: To enter a car; to arrive.
examples: Get in the car.
What time did you get in last night?
Our flight gets in at six.

spanish.definition: Entrar a un carro; llegar.

definition: To give something for free; to tell a secret.
examples: She gave away all her old clothes.
Don't give away the ending!
They're giving away free tickets.

spanish.definition: Dar algo gratis; contar un secreto.

definition: To return something.
examples: He gave back the money.
Please give back my phone.
He's giving back the money.

spanish.definition: Regresar algo.

definition: To stop fighting and accept what someone wants.
examples: My parents finally gave in.
Don't give in to them.
He never gives in.

spanish.definition: Dejar de pelear y aceptar lo que alguien quiere.

definition: To stop trying; to stop a habit.
examples: Don't give up!
He gave up smoking last year.
I'm not giving up on you.

spanish.definition: Dejar de intentar; dejar un hábito.

definition: To start or continue; used to give permission.
examples: Go ahead, take a cookie.
The game went ahead in the rain.
Can I sit here? Go ahead.

spanish.definition: Empezar o continuar; se usa para dar permiso.

definition: To leave a place; to disappear.
examples: Go away! I'm busy.
The pain went away after an hour.
We're going away for the weekend.

spanish.definition: Dejar un lugar; desaparecer.

definition: To check or review something.
examples: Let's go over the plan again.
We went over our notes before the test.
The teacher is going over the homework.

spanish.definition: Repasar o revisar algo.

definition: To become an adult.
examples: I grew up in Cali.
What do you want to be when you grow up?
Kids are growing up so fast.

spanish.definition: Volverse adulto.

definition: To give work to a teacher or a boss.
examples: Hand in your homework on Friday.
She handed in her resignation.
Everyone is handing in their tests.

spanish.definition: Dar un trabajo a un profesor o un jefe.

definition: To wait for a short time; to hold tightly.
examples: Hang on a minute!
Hang on tight!
She hung on to the rope.

spanish.definition: Esperar un momento; agarrarse fuerte.

definition: To spend time with friends in a relaxed way.
examples: We hung out at the mall.
Do you want to hang out this weekend?
The kids are hanging out in the park.

spanish.definition: Pasar tiempo con amigos de forma relajada.

definition: To end a phone call; to put something on a hook.
examples: Don't hang up on me!
She hung up the phone.
Hang up your coat.

spanish.definition: Terminar una llamada; poner algo en un gancho.

definition: To wait; to keep holding something.
examples: Hold on, I'll get my keys.
Hold on to the rail.
She held on to his arm.

spanish.definition: Esperar; seguir sosteniendo algo.

definition: To do something faster.
examples: Hurry up! The bus is coming.
She hurried up and finished.
Tell him to hurry up.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más rápido.

definition: To continue doing something.
examples: Keep on trying.
He kept on talking during the movie.
She keeps on calling me.

spanish.definition: Continuar haciendo algo.

definition: To move or work as fast as others; to continue.
examples: Keep up the good work!
I can't keep up with you.
She's keeping up with the class.

spanish.definition: Avanzar al mismo ritmo que otros; continuar.

definition: To start.
examples: The game kicks off at seven.
We kicked off the meeting with coffee.
The festival is kicking off tonight.

spanish.definition: Comenzar.

definition: To hit someone so they become unconscious.
examples: The boxer knocked out his opponent.
One punch knocked out the champion.
The storm knocked out the power.

spanish.definition: Golpear a alguien hasta dejarlo inconsciente.

definition: To end a worker's job because there isn't enough work.
examples: The factory laid off 200 workers.
He was laid off last month.
They're laying off staff.

spanish.definition: Quitarle el trabajo a alguien porque no hay suficiente trabajo.

definition: To not include someone or something.
examples: You left out an important detail.
She felt left out.
Don't leave anyone out.

spanish.definition: No incluir a alguien o algo.

definition: To disappoint someone.
examples: I felt let down by the movie.
I felt let down by my friends.
Don't let down your team.

spanish.definition: Fallarle a alguien.

definition: To put your body flat on a bed or the floor.
examples: I need to lie down.
She lay down on the sofa.
The dog is lying down by the door.

spanish.definition: Poner el cuerpo horizontal en una cama o el piso.

definition: To enter a computer system with a password.
examples: Log in with your email.
I can't log in to my account.
She logged in and checked her mail.

spanish.definition: Entrar a un sistema con una contraseña.

definition: To leave a computer system.
examples: Always log out on a public computer.
I logged out and closed the laptop.
Click here to log out.

spanish.definition: Salir de un sistema.

definition: To invent a story; to become friends again.
examples: He made up an excuse.
They had a fight, but they made up.
Stop making up stories!

spanish.definition: Inventar una historia; volver a ser amigos.

definition: To make a mistake; to make something dirty or untidy.
examples: I messed up the test.
The kids messed up the living room.
Don't mess this up!

spanish.definition: Cometer un error; ensuciar o desordenar algo.

definition: To start living in a new home.
examples: We moved in last week.
My girlfriend is moving in with me.
New neighbors moved in next door.

spanish.definition: Empezar a vivir en una casa nueva.

definition: To leave the place where you live.
examples: He moved out of his parents' house.
We have to move out by Friday.
She's moving out next month.

spanish.definition: Dejar el lugar donde vives.

definition: A polite way to say die.
examples: Her grandmother passed away last year.
He passed away peacefully.
I'm sorry your father passed away.

spanish.definition: Manera educada de decir morir.

definition: To become unconscious; to give things to people.
examples: He passed out from the heat.
The teacher passed out the tests.
She almost passed out.

spanish.definition: Perder el conocimiento; dar cosas a la gente.

definition: To return money you borrowed.
examples: I'll pay back the money tomorrow.
He paid back the loan.
She's still paying back her student loans.

spanish.definition: Regresar el dinero que pediste prestado.

definition: To choose.
examples: She picked out a red dress.
Help me pick out a gift.
We're picking out paint for the kitchen.

spanish.definition: Elegir.

definition: To lift something; to get someone in a car; to learn something easily.
examples: Pick up your toys.
Can you pick me up at the airport?
She picked up Spanish quickly.

spanish.definition: Levantar algo; recoger a alguien en carro; aprender algo con facilidad.

definition: To tell someone about something they didn't notice.
examples: She pointed out my mistake.
He pointed out the house where he was born.
I'd like to point out that it's late.

spanish.definition: Decirle a alguien algo que no había notado.

definition: To meet someone by chance; to hit something.
examples: I ran into my old teacher at the store.
The car ran into a tree.
We ran into some problems.

spanish.definition: Ver a alguien por casualidad; golpear algo.

definition: To use all of something.
examples: We ran out of milk.
I'm running out of time.
The money ran out.

spanish.definition: Usar todo lo que hay de algo.

definition: To start a business; to prepare equipment.
examples: She set up her own company.
Help me set up the tent.
We're setting up the chairs for the party.

spanish.definition: Empezar un negocio; preparar un equipo.

definition: To try to impress people.
examples: He's always showing off his car.
Stop showing off!
She showed off her new ring.

spanish.definition: Tratar de impresionar a la gente.

definition: To arrive.
examples: He showed up an hour late.
Only five people showed up.
She didn't show up for work.

spanish.definition: Llegar.

definition: A rude way to tell someone to stop talking.
examples: Shut up and listen!
He finally shut up.
Tell him to shut up.

spanish.definition: Manera grosera de pedirle a alguien que deje de hablar.

definition: To join a class or a group.
examples: I signed up for a yoga class.
Sign up on our website.
She's signing up for the trip.

spanish.definition: Apuntarse a una clase o un grupo.

definition: To move into a seat.
examples: Please sit down.
She sat down next to me.
Everyone is sitting down for dinner.

spanish.definition: Ponerse en un asiento.

definition: To go slower.
examples: Slow down! You're driving too fast.
The bus slowed down at the corner.
The economy is slowing down.

spanish.definition: Ir más despacio.

definition: To solve a problem; to organize.
examples: We need to sort out this mess.
She sorted out her closet.
I'm sorting out my papers.

spanish.definition: Arreglar un problema; ordenar.

definition: To talk louder; to say what you think.
examples: Please speak up; I can't hear you.
She spoke up for her friend.
You should speak up in meetings.

spanish.word: hablar más fuerte / alzar la voz
spanish.definition: Hablar más alto; decir lo que piensas.

definition: To get up onto your feet.
examples: Please stand up.
He stood up and left.
Everyone was standing up and clapping.

spanish.definition: Levantarse.

definition: To not go to bed.
examples: We stayed up all night.
Can I stay up late tonight?
She's staying up to finish her work.

spanish.definition: No acostarse a dormir.

definition: To think carefully about something.
examples: I need time to think over your offer.
She thought over his offer.
I'm thinking over the job.

spanish.definition: Pensar bien sobre algo.

definition: To put something in the trash.
examples: Don't throw away that box.
I threw away my old shoes.
She's throwing away the old newspapers.

spanish.definition: Poner algo en la basura.

definition: To vomit.
examples: I think I'm going to throw up.
The baby threw up on my shirt.
He's been throwing up all night.

spanish.definition: Sacar la comida del estómago por la boca.

definition: To put on clothes to see if they fit.
examples: Can I try on these shoes?
She tried on five dresses.
He's trying on a jacket.

spanish.definition: Ponerse ropa para ver si queda bien.

definition: To make louder; to appear.
examples: Turn up the music!
He turned up at my door.
Can you turn up the heat?

spanish.definition: Poner más alto; aparecer.

definition: To get ready for exercise; to make or become warmer.
examples: Warm up before you run.
I warmed up the soup.
The players are warming up.

spanish.definition: Prepararse para el ejercicio; hacer o volverse más cálido.

definition: To wash your hands and face.
examples: Go wash up before dinner.
He washed up and changed his shirt.
The kids are washing up.

spanish.definition: Lavarse las manos y la cara.

definition: To be careful.
examples: Watch out! There's a car coming.
Watch out for ice on the road.
She didn't watch out and fell.

spanish.definition: Andar con cuidado.

definition: To exercise; to find an answer; to end well.
examples: I work out at the gym every morning.
Don't worry, it'll work out.
Can you work out this math problem?

spanish.definition: Hacer ejercicio; encontrar una respuesta; terminar bien.

definition: To write something on paper.
examples: Write down my number.
I wrote down the address.
She's writing down everything he says.

spanish.definition: Escribir algo en papel.

definition: Belonging to her.
examples: This bag is hers.
Is that coat hers?
My car is red, and hers is blue.

spanish.definition: Que le pertenece a ella.

definition: Belonging to us.
examples: This house is ours.
Their dog is bigger than ours.
The choice is ours.

spanish.definition: Que nos pertenece.

definition: Belonging to them.
examples: The car is theirs.
Our kids are older than theirs.
That idea was theirs, not mine.

spanish.definition: Que les pertenece a ellos.

definition: An informal way to say thank you.
examples: Thanks for your help!
Thanks a lot.
Thanks, I'm fine.

spanish.definition: Manera informal de decir gracias.

definition: A sound that shows surprise, pleasure, or understanding.
examples: Ah, now I understand.
Ah, that feels good.
Ah, there you are!

spanish.definition: Sonido que muestra sorpresa, placer o comprensión.

definition: A sound you make when you are thinking.
examples: Hmm, let me think.
Hmm, that's a good question.
Hmm, I'm not sure.

spanish.definition: Sonido que haces cuando estás pensando.

definition: A word you shout when you are happy.
examples: Hooray! We won!
Hooray for summer!
The kids shouted hooray.

spanish.definition: Palabra que gritas cuando estás feliz.

definition: A word to show you are happy or excited.
examples: Yay! It's Friday!
We're going to the beach? Yay!
Yay, you're here!

spanish.definition: Palabra para mostrar que estás feliz o emocionado.

definition: A word to say food tastes good.
examples: Yum! This cake is great.
Yum, that smells good.
Pizza tonight? Yum!

spanish.definition: Palabra para decir que la comida sabe bien.

definition: A word to show you think something is disgusting.
examples: Yuck! This milk is bad.
Yuck, I hate broccoli.
There's a bug in my soup. Yuck!

spanish.definition: Palabra para mostrar que algo te da asco.

definition: Thin, crispy slices of fried potato sold in a bag.
examples: I'd like a bag of chips.
We had chips and salsa.
He ate the whole bag of chips.

spanish.definition: Rodajas delgadas y crujientes de papa frita que se venden en bolsa.

definition: A small round bread; hair tied in a round shape.
examples: Put the burger on a bun.
She wore her hair in a bun.
We bought hot dog buns.

spanish.definition: Pan pequeño y redondo; pelo recogido en forma redonda.

definition: A small ball of dough, often with meat inside.
examples: We ordered pork dumplings.
Her soup has chicken and dumplings.
I love Chinese dumplings.

spanish.definition: Bolita de masa, a menudo con carne adentro.

definition: An Italian dish of flat pasta, meat, and cheese.
examples: Mom made lasagna for dinner.
I'd like the vegetable lasagna.
This lasagna is delicious.

spanish.definition: Plato italiano de pasta plana, carne y queso.

definition: Ground meat cooked in the shape of a loaf.
examples: We had meatloaf and mashed potatoes.
My grandma makes the best meatloaf.
There's leftover meatloaf in the fridge.

spanish.definition: Carne molida cocinada en forma de pan.

definition: A sweet, soft food made with milk and eggs.
examples: She made a vanilla custard.
I love custard pie.
Serve the fruit with warm custard.

spanish.definition: Comida dulce y suave hecha con leche y huevos.

definition: Food cooked slowly in a deep dish in the oven.
examples: She brought a chicken casserole.
We had a tuna casserole for dinner.
Put the casserole in the oven.

spanish.definition: Comida cocinada despacio en un plato hondo en el horno.

definition: A small round green vegetable.
examples: Eat your peas.
She made pea soup.
We grow peas in the garden.

spanish.definition: Verdura pequeña, redonda y verde.

definition: A soft, sweet fruit with many small seeds.
examples: She ate a fresh fig.
We have a fig tree in the yard.
I love fig jam.

spanish.definition: Fruta suave y dulce con muchas semillas pequeñas.

definition: A tool with a heavy blade for cutting wood.
examples: He chopped the wood with an ax.
The firefighter broke the door with an ax.
Keep the ax in the shed.

spanish.definition: Herramienta con hoja pesada para cortar madera.
